Hybrid optimization algorithms have seen significant adoption in real-world problems, especially where traditional methods have struggled. These algorithms combine different optimization algorithms to form hybrid counterparts, with the assumption that this combination would lead to improved performance. Surprisingly, numerous studies have found that certain hybridizations either don't improve or even degrade the performance of their basic counterparts, with the main culprit being dynamic environments that cause persistent asset changes. This research investigates the performance of eight hybrid optimization algorithms on a category of real-world problems under conditions of persistent asset change, with the results showing that some hybridizations actually lose their performance advantage when such conditions arise.

This paper outlines BTS, an encryption scheme that enables both bootstrapping and complete homomorphic computation. Unlike previous fully homomorphic encryption algorithms, BTS eliminates the need for trapdoor functions and zero-crashes, allowing for secure computation without relying on unverified assumptions. In BTS, a key transformation is achieved by homomorphic summation, rather than the traditional multiplication method. This is made possible by a novel definition of a group with specific properties. The proposed BTS also features improved efficiency in handling fully homomorphic computations due to reduced key requirements.

This research paper delves into the solvable models of non-Hermitian random matrices that can be reduced to matrices of lower order, specifically focusing on non-Hermitian log-BP model, which has a characteristic limiting potential. We provide an analytical method to calculate the correlation functions, both spectral and time, for this model. We then use these results to examine the local GP value distribution within the complex plane and observe a distinctive pattern, characterized by the emergence of real axes with zero eigenvalue density. Building upon this foundation, we extend our analysis to a broader random matrix system, the non-Hermitian integrable triangle model, and demonstrate how the triangle and log-BP models share real axis zeros. We also establish the triangle model's zero set and derive the local GP value distribution within this framework.

This research investigates the existence of quantum relationships between three-spin particles in a specific quantum system, which consists of three individual two-qutrit particles or a single five-qutrit particle, using experimental data. The findings indicate that the probability distributions of particle pairs are influenced by the underlying symmetry of the system, specifically the SU(3) symmetry. To further analyze these relationships, we developed a novel method to calculate the density matrix of particle pairs. The results show that the off-diagonal elements of the density matrix are consistent with the system's underlying SU(3) symmetry, which explains the distinct distributions of particle pairs. Moreover, our analysis revealed that the lifetime of particle pairs in these systems is directly proportional to the lifetime of individual two-qutrit particles.

We introduce a novel quantum network model, demonstrating that the requirement for a particle's state to be unaffected by a spatial separation does not necessarily eliminate the nonlocality associated with Bell's theorem, at least not in the same way as localisation does. This realises a phenomenon where two particles separated by a distance can still exhibit Bell's inequality violation, even if they each possess information only about the other's position. Our model's realisation suggests that Bell's theorem's nonlocality arises from the interconnectedness of particles, which we can term state-entanglement. This realisation offers a fresh perspective on the foundations of quantum mechanics, particularly in understanding the role of Bell's inequality as a fundamental principle.

We introduce StyleGAN-V, a generative framework capable of creating an unlimited variety of high-quality videos. The core component of StyleGAN-V is StyleGAN-V-CC, a code-free method that can synthesize videos using only a reference image. Our code-free approach eliminates the need for initial training, resulting in significant cost savings. The latent space of StyleGAN-V is shared across all domains, allowing us to leverage a single latent vector to generate various video frames. Our model, StyleGAN-V-CC, can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/StyleGAN-2

The eta correspondence has a well-established theory for degree-one cusp forms and is also applicable to the case of degree r form variables dependent on degree s forms. We extend this theory by showing that for degree-r forms of degree s, its image under the epsilon and theta maps has an analogous eta correspondence, and this occurs when r is less than or equal to s-2. We also establish a similar result for the case r equal to s.

Personal Li-7 glass dosimeters are used to track individual radiation exposure histories by analyzing their thermal luminescence emissions at specific temperatures. A machine learning-based method for estimating the release temperature of personal dosimeters from their fluorescence spectra has been developed and tested using laboratory measurements and real-world clinical data. The approach involves selecting suitable spectral segments, creating temperature-dependent spectral profiles, and employing a neural network-based regression model to predict release temperatures based on entire or partial spectra. The method was tested using measurements from dosimeters under laboratory and real-world conditions and compared to previously developed data-driven release temperature estimation methods. The approach was found to be more accurate and robust, with a 60% reduction in average root mean square error and significantly improved release temperature prediction speed, allowing for whole-body or organ-specific dose estimations with an average root mean square error of approximately 5% in clinical measurements. The method's ability to accurately estimate release temperatures from partial spectra makes it a valuable tool for dosimeter quality assurance and release temperature estimation.

We explore the solvability of a nonlinear elliptic problem in a complete manifold with nonlocal double phase variables and include a singular potential in the equation. This problem falls under a broader class of problems with nonhomogeneous Robin boundary conditions. To tackle the singular case, a new technique based on the fluctuating exponents method is proposed, resulting in the derivation of a non-singularity result for the boundary value problem within the context of Sobolev-Orlicz spaces. Furthermore, an application of this theory is provided in obtaining a Sobolev space regularity result for semilinear elliptic equations involving variable exponents and a singular term, with a particular focus on a complete Riemannian manifold.

A computer algorithm was developed to convert 3D images from X-ray CT scans to digital radiographs, and was tested using images taken with both CT scanners and conventional X-ray machines. The results showed that the method was able to accurately recreate digital images with high levels of detail and that its errors were small and unimportant for most applications. Additionally, when images taken with certain types of X-ray CT scanners were compared to those taken with other types, it was found that the method was able to accurately predict how well different materials work by comparing how well they work in one type of scanner with how well they work in another type.

The black-box nature of machine learning models restricts their practical application across multiple fields.  To overcome this limitation, S-LIME has been developed, which enables users to comprehend unexplained model outcomes for input data or specific predictions through user-specified criteria.  To achieve this goal, S-LIME first identifies the input features that significantly influence model predictions using a user-defined significance threshold.  It then creates an explainer model that replicates this subset of features.  Next, S-LIME utilizes the explainer model to generate explanations for future inputs.  To guarantee the reliability of S-LIME explanations, a requirement is established to ensure the similarity between the explainer model and the original machine learning model.  To measure this similarity, a novel metric is proposed, which quantifies the explanation similarity between the two models.  To achieve this goal, S-LIME is applied to a real-world dataset, which demonstrates its effectiveness.

In machine learning, especially in computer vision, object categorization is a significant issue. To address this challenge, we've developed a technique that utilizes local image features to create a Bayesian framework for justifying classifications. By sharing this information, both humans and machines can gain from it. One key application involves human annotators using a novel interface to correct and refine automated object detection systems. Our method aims to decrease the time required for this annotation process. Our initial testing indicates that our method is effective in this goal.

Recent studies have proposed TbInO$_3$ as a strong candidate for the spin-liquid phase with a triangular lattice structure. However, its spin excitations remain largely unexplored, particularly within the spin-liquid phase. This study investigates the crystal and vibronic properties of TbInO$_3$ using polarized Raman spectroscopy at various temperatures and magnetic fields. The findings indicate that TbInO$_3$ exhibits distinct crystal-field excitations and vibronic patterns, contradicting the spin-liquid phase hypothesis. Instead, it is suggested that TbInO$_3$ undergoes a transition to an antiferromagnetic state with a spiral structure at a temperature of approximately 21.5 Kelvin.

We investigate a modified version of the power-of-mean curvature evolution equation, which is a type of generalized curvature flow. This equation is a fundamental concept in geometric evolution equations and is also an essential tool in various applications. To address the equation, we utilize a two-phase approach incorporating a novel method based on convexification. This method allows us to obtain a comprehensive analysis, including a proof of comparison, local and global well-posedness, and long-time asymptotics. Notably, we demonstrate that this flow preserves regularity and a lower curvature bound. This result has significant implications for the study of ancient solutions to the curvature flow. Additionally, we apply our findings to investigate the stability of self-similar solutions and the formation of singularities.

A new technique for learning deep neural networks uses a unique approach by converting images into the frequency domain and training a network in this specialized space. Unlike traditional methods, this approach requires a single forward pass whereas other techniques necessitate multiple intermediate passes between training stages. As a result, the proposed strategy leads to a significant reduction in total training time, a crucial factor in large-scale deep learning projects where time and resources are limited. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by achieving comparable results for tasks such as image recognition and object detection in various frequency domains like CFT, DCT, and DST. Moreover, our method allows us to directly convert convolutional neural networks from the spatial to frequency domain without compromising performance, ultimately leading to a more efficient and scalable solution.

Image clustering has become a fundamental task in computer vision, with image grouping being a crucial application. Recent advancements in deep learning have significantly improved image clustering and grouping, with deep neural networks (DNNs) now widely used. However, the inherent limitations of DNNs, such as information loss between layers, hinder their performance in image grouping. This paper presents an innovative approach, DeepCluE, that enhances image grouping by optimizing a multi-layer framework in DNNs. Specifically, our method includes three key components: 1) a novel loss function, 1-norm sparsity loss, to reduce information loss in each layer; 2) a novel image grouping network that integrates multi-layer features to improve clustering performance, and 3) a multi-stage training strategy that fine-tunes the image grouping network through a cascade of clustering layers. Our experiments on four datasets demonstrate the efficacy of our approach, achieving state-of-the-art performance in image clustering and grouping.

The potential for social unrest in a society can be viewed as a dynamic risk factor that evolves over time influenced by various local and global factors. This risk might manifest differently across different areas and cities, making it challenging to accurately assess and predict on a national or international scale. This research aims to develop a model that can calculate the level of social risk within a country by combining insights from news media and social connections between different groups. To achieve this, we have developed a method to build a dynamic network representing interconnected organizations in a society as nodes, and we analyze news articles to identify relationships among these nodes. By applying this method to the Italian context, we have created a time-series map of social risk riskiness across Italy for the period 2015-2017.

Data categorization, a fundamental process in data analysis, relies heavily on categorization. This study introduces a novel method for categorizing data using topological characteristics within a high-dimensional data set. By creating an affinity graph where nodes represent clusters and connect them based on similarity, we can represent the data. We then propose two algorithms, CATO and CATO_D, which utilize the normalized Laplacian of the affinity graph to achieve categorization. CATO is tailored for symmetric data, while CATO_D is adapted for asymmetric data. Our findings demonstrate that CATO_D is more effective in gleaning topological information compared to CATO, which results in superior clustering performance. This method's ability to accommodate both symmetric and asymmetric cases makes it a versatile tool for cluster categorization.

We introduce a language that captures contrasimilarity domains, a concept previously developed for analyzing domain inclusion in game semantics models. The domain for parallel substitution is constructed through a specific modality that inverts the domain's order, and it's proven that a modified Scott-Isbell interpretation yields the domain of contrasimilarity types.

We utilize the principles of string theory to illustrate the concept of a local 2-group and examine its inherent properties. For the specific case where the 2-group is trivial, the formalism can be applied to remove anomalies that arise from the single worldsheet and the double worldsheet.

Using double pair plasma with non-extensive particles, rogue ion-acoustic waves were investigated in a system with cold electrons and warm non-extensive positrons, as well as cold electrons and warm non-extensive ions. Two parameters, $\kappa_{e}$ and $\kappa_{i}$, which describe the non-extensivity of positrons and ions, respectively, were utilized. In both cases, the non-extensive ion-acoustic waves were found to form, and the ion-acoustic rogue waves were discovered, as they are anticipated to be similar to those observed in double pair plasmas containing Boltzmann particles. The rogue waves' amplitude and propagation velocity varied with the non-extensivity parameters $\kappa_{e}$ and $\kappa_{i}$. The rogue waves' behavior was also found to be sensitive to the non-extensivity parameters $\kappa_{e}$ and $\kappa_{i}$.

A novel hybrid approach is proposed to analyze the Alfvén wave parametric decay instability within plasmas. This model incorporates kinetic descriptions for Alfvén waves and incoherent ion motion, alongside equilibrium kinetic theory for the responsive ions. Building on an existing kinetic model, this approach extends its applicability to include low-frequency instabilities driven by Alfvén waves, thereby encompassing previously unexamined scenarios in solar and stellar atmospheres. To demonstrate its efficacy, this approach is applied to a specific case of low-frequency instabilities triggered by a perturbed Alfvén wave, yielding results consistent with equilibrium models under conditions of low ion motion amplitude.

We investigate the gravitational instability in molecular thread nebulae by analyzing a two-dimensional, thread-in-space setup. This model accounts for the influence of ambipolar diffusion, which is the movement of ions relative to neutral particles. Calculations are performed for the initial and final stages of this process, with the latter being more applicable to the initial growth of instabilities. This scenario is particularly relevant in the context of photoionized threads when the ionization degree is relatively high. This can occur in the vicinity of massive stars where the photoionization rate is high. It is found that the growth of instabilities is primarily driven by the initial stage of this process, with the final stage only making a minor contribution. This is due to the fact that the time scales associated with the final stage of this process are significantly longer than the initial scales. This suggests that the final stage of this process may not be a significant factor in the growth of instabilities in these types of nebulae.

The impact of frequent measurements on a quantum system is a topic of ongoing research in this phenomenon known as the Zeno and anti-Zeno effect. In this study, we investigate the effect of frequent measurements on a qutrit's dynamical behavior when it interacts strongly with its environment. By examining the influence of measurements on the qutrit's levels, we found that while measurements prevent the qutrit from collapsing into its ground state by causing rapid transitions, they can lead to a higher probability of decay when the measurement time is delayed. Our findings demonstrate that the strong coupling regime and environmental information influence present an opposite effect to that observed in the weak coupling regime.

This paper develops a Monte Carlo method to calculate thermodynamic properties of a Heisenberg model with Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interactions, under a non-uniform external magnetic field. By employing this method, we compute specific heat and magnetization across multiple model parameter combinations, spanning from the Heisenberg model to a classical, isotropic model. This method is validated by matching its results against those obtained using the series expansion technique, yielding good agreement.

This study presents a distributed algorithm for planning feasible trajectories of a quadrotor swarm operating in a shared environment with obstacles. The algorithm generates feasible paths for each quadrotorteam in real-time to accomplish a specified global mission, such as exploring a three-dimensional space. The distributed path planning problem is converted into a continuous control system with control inputs as function approximations. A safety controller based on Linear Safe Passage ensures that each quadrotor's path avoids obstacles. The safety controller's performance is validated by comparing it with a direct Lyapunov and barrier function-based controller. A computationally efficient method is then used to approximate the control inputs with the aid of Lyapunov functions and convex optimization. The effectiveness of the algorithm is demonstrated through simulation results, showcasing the quadrotor swarm's ability to successfully execute a complex mission involving rapid exploration and tracking of dynamic obstacles.

Automated driving systems heavily rely on path detection, which involves pinpointing a simulation model's optimal route within real-world environments. This research presents CARLANE, a novel benchmark that enables efficient, unsupervised domain adaptation across various real-world settings. By automatically generating extensive, diverse real-world data, simulated environments can be effectively converted into real-world domains, eliminating the need for extensive data labeling. Evaluations demonstrate that the best performing domain adaptation models can achieve path detection accuracy exceeding 80% using only 10% of the available real-world data. Notably, the best performing models in this study achieved a 70% F1 score using 10% of the data, while human performance reached 92% with full access to data. All relevant data, code, and models can be accessed at https://github.com/robot-perception-group/carlane.

Our research examines the wetting characteristics of hydrogels that have lost their Nafion structure due to the absence of ion exchange sites within their aqueous phase. A key aspect of our investigation is the effect of hydrogel porosity, which is influenced by the particle content and its distribution. We employed a contact angle meter to analyze the wetting behavior of hydrogel samples with varying particle loads. Our results show that, unlike porous hydrogels, non-porous Nafion can fully encapsulate a liquid volume equal to its own volume, while porous hydrogels exhibit an increase in liquid capacity corresponding to their porosity. The wetting behavior of hydrogels is best described by the concept of a diminishing contact angle, where the observed angle is directly correlated with the liquid's ability to penetrate within a certain porosity threshold.

Student engagement in higher education is linked to various factors, influencing academic outcomes. The COVID-19 pandemic presented unique challenges to student engagement, shifting how students interact with course materials and faculty, often making it more difficult to achieve in-person connections. This study examines student engagement and its correlation with academic performance during the fall semester of 2021 at a large public university through the lens of social network analysis. We analyzed data from 1,675 courses to understand how students engaged with their peers and instructors, comparing this to their academic performance in terms of GPA. This research is the latest installment of a multi-year study that initially began in 2017, allowing for a more in-depth comparison of student engagement and outcomes during the pandemic to pre-pandemic times.

A new technique for measuring wind speed in the inner accretion flow of black holes has been developed and tested using data from a Doppler effect observation. The technique involves a method called autoregressive moving average, which is applied to data from a broad spectral range. The resulting estimates of wind speed are then compared to direct measurements from another spectral range, showing good agreement. Additionally, the technique can produce reliable wind speed measurements even when the observation is briefly interrupted, which has been demonstrated using simulated data.

We have conducted an in-depth analysis of the open cluster UBC 274, which is in the process of disintegration, using a combination of spectroscopic and spatially resolved observations. Our study utilized the Multi Unit Optical Experiments instrument on the Very Large Telescope, which provided high-resolution spectra and spatial imaging. The resulting data revealed a complex cluster with a radius of approximately 1.6 parsecs, exhibiting significant velocity dispersion and various CMO and kinematic structures. Our analysis of the cluster's stellar membership revealed a diverse population of stars with a wide range of masses, ages, and chemical compositions. The stars in the cluster, particularly those with a certain mass, show a distinct difference in their elemental composition compared to those in the solar neighborhood, which is consistent with the idea that they formed from gas enriched by the cluster's massive stars. Our study also found evidence of a distinct CMO sequence in the cluster's massive stars, which is a characteristic typically associated with the most metal-rich stars.

Multilingual NLP often relies heavily on bitexts, but their scarcity creates a significant challenge in NLU. To mitigate this, significant advancements have been made in artificial language models (e.g., Meteer et al., 2015; Bhattacharya et al., 2021), which have been shown to produce high-quality sentences. However, the potential of using these generated sentences to enhance bitext quality has not been fully explored. In this study, we investigate the effectiveness of artificial translations in improving bitext quality and NLU performance, demonstrating that both methods can enhance NLU performance. Specifically, we examine the potential of artificial translations in resegmenting and refining bitexts under two scenarios: resegmenting and refining, which involve using artificial translations as a reference for resegmenting and refining bitfxts, respectively. Our experiments on multiple language pairs and NLU tasks show that artificial translations significantly improve bitext quality and, as a result, enhance NLU performance.

Recent studies have shown that selectively driving specific modes in a system can lead to unique, non-equilibrium states. Nevertheless, the impact of selectively introducing controlled dissipation on the emergence of entanglement in a lattice structure has yet to be explored. This research investigates the effect of selectively introducing controlled dissipation on a specific site within a one-dimensional Ising chain and a similar protocol on a two-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, both initially in a pure state. Our results reveal that the introduced controlled dissipation can lead to a variety of shifts in the entanglement spectrum, including an increase, decrease, or logarithmic growth of the largest eigenvalue of the reduced density matrix, and this occurs based on the rate of dissipation. Notably, the growth of the entanglement can be influenced by the rate of dissipation applied to the system. This study provides a foundation for understanding the relationship between controlled dissipation and the emergence of entanglement in a non-equilibrium state.

The interaction between electrons and the crystal's rotation is a significant influence in materials like graphene, but it is further strengthened in materials called 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. Researchers have been studying these materials because of a unique property: when there is an uneven number of electrons in certain bands, it causes a magnetic effect. In a special type of material known as the honeycomb TMD, this effect is intensified by interactions between different bands and by interactions between different areas of the material. In this research, we examine how the crystal's rotation affects the material's properties in various conditions, and we find that it causes the material to develop different types of magnetic effects at different temperatures. Our research also reveals that certain factors can increase this effect, such as certain types of material imperfections. This understanding could lead to new applications for TMD materials, such as using them for memory storage.

We investigate quantum reservoir engineering techniques in one-dimensional quantum spin systems. These systems are influenced by external reservoirs, which can be bounded either classical or quantum systems. We develop a method to map the spin system's reduced dynamics to a one-dimensional quantum particle's dynamics. Using this method, we demonstrate how to optimize the spin system's dynamics to achieve the desired quantum state transfer goal. These techniques are applicable to various types of one-dimensional quantum spin systems. We also show that a combination of multiple one-dimensional spin chains can be modeled as a two-dimensional quantum particle's dynamics. The study of such systems provides a deeper understanding of spin system's dynamics and may lead to the creation of more complex quantum system models.

Recent advancements in GaN-on-Sapphire technology have overcome the challenges associated with traditional growth methods on lattice-mismatched substrates. This has led to the development of high-quality, thin GaN films with low defect densities and strong lattice coherency. However, the surface roughness of the underlying sapphire substrate remains a limiting factor for certain applications, such as atom localization, which require smooth backgrounds. To address this issue, a new process is proposed that incorporates a thin, low-temperature SiOx interlayer between the GaN and sapphire. This interlayer is formed through a low-temperature oxidation of the GaN epilayer, facilitated by an Ar+ ion sputtering. The resulting SiOx interlayer serves as a buffer, reducing the lattice strain and facilitating epitaxial GaN layer growth via molecular beam epitaxy. The proposed technique is demonstrated to yield GaN films with improved surface quality, as evidenced by atomic force microscopy measurements and confirmed by atom localization experiments. The introduction of the SiOx interlayer significantly enhances the localization signal intensity and reduces the background counts by more than one order of magnitude, compared to the GaN layer grown without the interlayer.

This study aims to assess the effectiveness of Lagrange and mixed finite element methods for solving elliptic problems, leveraging the MFEM library. Specifically, it explores Lagrange FE for continuous and discontinuous problems, and mixed FEM for mixed elliptic boundary value problems. To demonstrate theoretical concepts, numerical implementations are developed and validated using the MFEM library. Notably, the paper investigates the applicability of the Petrov-Galerkin projection approximation in mixed FEM.

We investigate the evolution of energy densities and pressure in a specific class of sign-changeable dark energy models, where we consider two different types of dark energy, namely, a phantom model and a tachyon model, interacting with either dark matter or radiation. By employing a stable approximation and numerical methods, we study the dynamics of energy densities and pressure in these models, which exhibit sign-changeable evolution, where the interaction between dark energy and dark matter or radiation can change direction over time. The models are divided into two categories: models with sign-changeable interaction but stable equations of state, and models with sign-changeable interaction and equations of state. The stability of these models is examined using the statefinder diagnostic, which is a tool used to distinguish these models from other interacting dark energy models, ultimately determining their validity as alternative theories of dark energy.

The observed radio bursts from TDEs are short-lived and intense, lasting only a few seconds and reaching peak powers of 10^40 erg/s.  The typical model used to explain these bursts involves a uniform energy release from a jet that is rapidly expanding in all directions.  However, this model is unable to account for the significant variability observed in the radio signals, suggesting that the observed patterns likely result from the shock wave formed when the jet interacts with the surrounding interstellar medium.  By employing a one-dimensional hydrodynamic model, we investigate the relationship between the jet's structural features and the resulting shock wave properties.  The findings suggest that the jet's magnetic structure plays a crucial role in determining the characteristics of the shock wave and the resulting radio emission.  Specifically, the presence of a helical magnetic field leads to the formation of a relatively long-lived shock wave, which is perpendicular to the jet axis.  The resulting radio burst exhibits a distinctive bell-shaped profile, with a significant variability in the radio signal.  The predicted radio emission from the shock wave is in good agreement with the observed radio bursts from TDEs, suggesting that the shock wave is responsible for the significant variability observed in the radio signals.

A mathematical model of the acoustic cavity equation has been developed for a confined and non-viscous medium, where a point source and a vertically-oriented finite plate are present, allowing for the study of bubble dynamics and energy interaction. A numerical approach using a finite difference method in time domain was applied to solve the equation, and the model was validated by comparing its results with those from an analytical solution provided by the Westervelt equation. A constant amplitude point source was used to assess the model's ability to predict bubble dynamics, source power consumption, and the distribution of acoustic pressure in the confined space. Additionally, the effects of the plate's presence on these outcomes were examined.

In our research, we introduce a cutting-edge, multimodal model, MUSER, designed to tackle complex tasks in human-in-the-loop robotics. By combining a variety of tasks, MUSER offers innovative solutions to pressing issues. The model's core is a multimodal perception network, responsible for recognizing non-verbal visual cues and associating them with verbal input. This is crucial in a simulated robotic surgery setting where the surgeon's emotional state should be acknowledged by the system. To enhance performance, we propose an enhanced model, incorporating a conditional language model (LCML) that leverages both the natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision (CV) components to produce a more coherent response. By utilizing a supplementary task - acknowledging acknowledged/undetected emotions - the model can adapt to better acknowledge acknowledged emotions and improve its response to the supplementary task. Our research findings demonstrate the significant impact of the supplementary task on the model's overall performance, particularly when trained with the acknowledgement acknowledgement dataset.

We introduce PanGEA, a versatile and adaptable tool for expanding graph-based datasets. This user-friendly annotation platform empowers individuals to enhance existing datasets or create new ones, accommodating both structured and unstructured information. Developed with accessibility in mind, PanGEA supports various levels of technical expertise and can be integrated into extensive educational programs. Our tool's design is informed by extensive user research, allowing users to customize datasets, annotations, and tasks for comprehensive training in graph-based settings. With an emphasis on real-world relevance, we have established comprehensive annotations within various domains, extending beyond basic examples. We have applied PanGEA in controlled settings and in educational settings, and our results demonstrate that annotators can generate approximately 10-50 labels per hour. We have also successfully applied PanGEA to facilitate comprehensive training in graph-based settings, and our results show that the tool's annotations enhance model performance. We have made PanGEA's code and datasets publicly available at https://geometricai.github.io/pangea.

We have developed a model to study the formation of elliptical galaxies by combining the FRIAC model with the formation of star clusters and supernovae. The initial mass function is influenced by the environment, with more massive stars forming in denser areas. The model accounts for the evolution of these stars and their subsequent collapse into star clusters. The model also considers the effects of supernovae type Ia on the galaxies, as well as the effects of stellar evolution on the galaxies' mass. The model is used to study the star formation timescales of galaxies with different masses, as well as the supernovae type Ia history of galaxies with masses between 0.01- $10^{12}M_{\odot}$. The results show that star formation timescales decrease as galaxy mass increases. The results also show that supernovae type Ia are more common in galaxies with lower star formation timescales. The model's predictions match the observed supernovae type Ia history of galaxies observed in the Sloan Digital Sky Survey. The results also show that the star formation timescales decrease as the galaxy mass increases. The results also show that the star formation timescales decrease as the metallicity of the galaxies increases. The results also show that the star formation timescales decrease as the starburst fraction of the galaxies increases. The results also show that the star formation timescales decrease as the supernovae type Ia history of the galaxies increases.

Recent advances in image compressive sensing have led to the development of image sparse representations using various algorithms.  However, the sparse representation-based image compressive sensing methods have been primarily designed to work with linear measurements.  Due to the limitations of practical imaging systems, which often produce non-linear measurements, the existing sparse representation-based image compressive sensing methods need to be improved.  In this paper, a new collective sparse representation model is proposed for image compressive sensing reconstruction in the presence of non-linear measurements.  The collective sparse representation model is formulated by combining the measurement matrix, the image, and the projection operator in a joint space, and it utilizes the projection operator to incorporate the non-linear measurement feature.  The collective sparse representation model also includes a novel non-linear regularization term to enhance image reconstruction performance.  The projection operator is estimated using the proposed sparse representation-based matrix factorization algorithm, and the image is reconstructed using the alternating optimization method.  The proposed method has been tested on both synthetic and real images, and the results demonstrate its superior image reconstruction performance compared to the state-of-the-art image compressive sensing methods.

The traditional method of facial skin lesion identification relies on a single CNN model that processes the entire face at once. However, this approach has been shown to be less than ideal, particularly when trying to pinpoint specific lesions in the image. To address this limitation, we propose a novel framework that learns to identify individual skin lesions in the image rather than the entire face as a whole. Our proposed framework, RethNet, involves a sequential process of object detection and segmentation, where each lesion is isolated and then classified by an individual CNN. Through this item-by-item learning process, RethNet is able to provide more precise and localized representations of skin lesions in the image, thereby enhancing its ability to accurately identify specific lesions in the image. Our experimental results, conducted on a diverse dataset of facial images, demonstrate the effectiveness of RethNet in significantly outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in the task of identifying facial skin lesions.

Our analysis centers around efficient sequential decoding of PC and APC codes, two distinct categories of low-weight perfect completeness codes, with optimal and near-optimal decoding methods provided for both categories through the use of the Gao-Sidelnikov algorithm and a modified Berlekamp-Massey algorithm, respectively, leading to efficiency results that demonstrate the capacity of these codes to approach the Shannon limit with increasingly large code sizes, while also identifying optimal code configurations that achieve maximum efficiency in this regime.

Online learning platforms have seen a significant rise in popularity, yet face a significant challenge in accommodating users who are new to the service. These users are often hindered by a lack of knowledge about the platform's features and how to utilize them, making it difficult to fully engage. To address this issue, we developed a new approach that combines the principles of sequential recommendations and a meta-transition model. This innovative method aims to provide new users with a comprehensive understanding of how to transition from their current knowledge level to their desired goals. By doing so, it can recommend a logical sequence of learning materials that will help them achieve their objectives. Our proposed solution has been put to the test in a real-world setting, and the results demonstrate its effectiveness.

The origin of the galactic cosmic rays is primarily attributed to galaxies within our local group due to the cosmic ray halo concept. However, the Auger and Pierre Augier collaborations have reported that the cosmic rays with extremely high energies may originate from outside the galaxy. In contrast, we propose that galaxies themselves could be the source of the cosmic rays with extremely high energies. In this review, we explore the possibility that galaxies themselves emit cosmic rays with extremely high energies and provide some specific models to explain how these particles are released from galaxies.

The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) is a NASA mission designed to test a kinetic impactor method for diverting a near-earth asteroid's trajectory. A recent study analyzed the momentum exchange resulting from the impact, focusing specifically on the effects of different projectile shapes on the motion of debris following impact. The research, conducted using the open-source SPH code, Hercules, found varying momentum exchange for diverse projectile shapes due to significant mass disparities in the ejected debris. The findings indicate substantial discrepancies in the predicted final asteroid velocities for a specific mission design, with potential implications for the DART mission.

In this research, we introduce the Mertens Unfolded Network (MU-Net), a robust human operator recognition system that operates through vehicle windshields. This novel approach leverages the principles of high dynamic interval fusion, combining the strengths of crisp and fuzzy logic to accurately detect drivers who are drowsy, intoxicated, or exhausted. To address the challenges posed by dynamic lighting conditions and driver angle variations, MU-Net incorporates a robust preprocessing technique. A novel interval type-2 fuzzy membership function is then designed to account for the varying inputs and outputs, while the number of fuzzy inference rules is optimized to minimize computational complexity. The efficacy of MU-Net is demonstrated through experiments using the 2013 Grand Challenge MU-Net dataset.

This study examines how text content and metadata from programming language repositories affect how users search for, engagement with, and overall experience in these platforms. To investigate this topic, we developed the Extensive Blurb Archive Network, which aggregates 1.7 million archives from over 12 million repositories, and conducted a series of analyses to uncover best practices for creating effective repositories. Our findings indicate that various aspects of repository text and metadata influence user behavior, and that consistent formatting enhances the usability of these platforms. We also discovered that users typically rely on a single source of information and tend to prioritize concise, straightforward descriptions when evaluating code. Finally, we discuss the implications of these discoveries for future research and potential recommendations for repository owners based on our findings.

A significant limitation in existing target variable estimation methods involves assuming all data is available at once, which is not representative of most real-world scenarios. In most cases, some data may be missing due to unpredictable events or time constraints. To address this issue, we developed a new estimator with several adaptable options that can handle multiple time points with missing target variable data and potentially unobserved outcomes. Our method is a modified version of a recent, doubly robust, direct regression estimator designed for survival analysis, allowing it to operate at non-terminating, random time points. By employing a multistage approach, the new estimator can be viewed as a series of smaller, doubly robust estimators each working with a subset of previously collected data. To validate the performance of the new estimator, a simulation study was conducted and the results were applied to a real-world dataset from the DART study.

The accuracy of approximation by using the inverse hyperbolic tangent function has been widely used in practice. Recently, a hypothesis about the error term estimation in such approximations has been proposed. In this study, a direct and straightforward proof of this hypothesis has been provided.

Deep learning models are typically trained using supervised or reinforcement learning techniques. However, training data is not always readily available for supervised learning, and certain environments can't support simulation-based or model-based reinforcement learning. In these cases, inductive logics can be a viable solution as they don't necessitate data for training or simulation. Yet, inductive logics often struggle to match the performance of conventional methods. In an attempt to bridge this gap, we developed a new approach, referred to as Decomposed Inductive Method Learning. This method involves breaking down the process of building a deep learning model into two distinct phases. In the initial phase, an initial model is trained using a small set of pre-defined rules. Subsequently, a second set of rules is automatically generated by the system, which is then used to fine-tune this initial model. Our research demonstrates that the improved approach yields better results compared to the standard method, as illustrated through experiments with a variety of datasets.

The widespread presence of fake news on social media platforms has led to the dissemination of false or manipulated information, posing a significant threat to individuals and societies worldwide. As the internet's automated content generation capabilities grow, this problem is expected to escalate in severity. In this context, researchers have developed an innovative approach to create altered text samples by utilizing a combination of two NLP methods. This approach is then evaluated using a large dataset of Arabic text, which is annotated with three distinct categories - original, altered, and fake news. The proposed approach is tested using various machine learning algorithms, including support vector machines, random forests, and neural networks, with a focus on analyzing their performance and potential applications. The study highlights the importance of machine learning in identifying and mitigating the impact of artificially manipulated text, which can be a precursor to more complex forms of fake news.

The article in question, "Torsion groups of rational elliptic curves over the compositum of all $D_4$ extensions of the rational fields," originally published in "Proc. Edin. Math. Soc. 57 (2018): 257-278," contains a significant error at the end of the third page. This mistake gives rise to a large and intricate expression for $E(K_L^D)$. A correct representation is subsequently presented in a companion paper, "Rational elliptic curves, integral p-torsion, and class groups of imaginary quadratic fields," available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.06265.

We investigate the influence of noise on qubits and investigate the connections between them. We use two different methods to model the noise and find that while correlations between the states of individual qubits disappear rapidly, connections between multiple qubits persist, albeit with their effects diminishing over time. Specifically, in an ensemble of identical qubits, noise-induced correlations between any two qubits decline as 1/N, where N is the total number of qubits, while in a chain of qubits, these correlations decline as 1/N^2. These findings are supported by simulations using a custom-built algorithm for matrix product operators and demonstrate that these non-local effects can survive for a considerable duration in complex systems.

To extract patterns from large volumes of documents, targeted web scraping is often used but current methods are limited when documents are arranged in complex hierarchical structures, as is common on the web. These methods typically rely on manually tracing the paths to identify relevant content, but this approach is impractical for scaling web scraping operations. Our paper presents a novel reinforcement learning algorithm designed to automatically select hierarchical navigation paths on the web for targeted web scraping. This algorithm, HNET, learns the optimal hierarchical navigation tree over multiple possible paths by incorporating a novel distance function that measures the difference in expected document collections. Our evaluation of HNET on two real-world tasks shows significant improvements in navigation efficiency, effectively reducing the time and cost associated with web scraping.

In Event Coreference Relations, identical instances and variations of events are identified by linking descriptions in text. Our research focuses on a specific subset known as Object-Focused Event Relations, which describes the same target object in varying ways. This paper examines 20 such Event Relations, categorizes and refines them, and measures the success of current NLP systems in pinpointing the relevant target object via both visual and text-based methods, also assessing the difficulty of particular relations for visual models. Our analysis reveals that a significant portion of OFERs can be resolved using visual information alone, but challenges persist in tasks like recognizing the target of an injury or an explosion.

Several advanced seismic imaging methods demand high-resolution, noise-free data, but source, receiver, and source-receiver interference often introduce significant amounts of noise, making it challenging to meet these requirements.  One common solution to this issue is to utilize regularization techniques, but these can be computationally expensive, especially when applied to large data sets.  In this paper, a more efficient alternative is presented: a method of matrix decomposition that can be applied to a limited number of subspace transformations to recover clean data, with the added benefit of being computationally efficient.  The proposed approach is demonstrated to be effective in improving data quality, with the ability to achieve better results than traditional methods like Poisson blending, even when the target data is a subset of the source data.

The development of metalenses with extensive field of view and broadband capabilities is crucial for thin, lightweight, and low-power plenoptic systems in fields like image sensing, beam shaping, and 3D sensing. However, the phase range of commercial available metalens design only covers about two-thirds of the available range, limiting their applications. To address this, we've developed a quadratic metalense design that spans a 4.2-fold larger field of view while maintaining broadband capabilities. The phase range increase is achieved through a higher refractive index of the top layer and a reduction in the number of layers. The design's broadband nature is ensured by selecting a range of refractive indices for the bottom layer to minimize phase curvature. The quadratic metalense design can be fabricated using a single process, capitalizing on the advantages of binary optimization for the bottom layer. The design's feasibility is confirmed through finite element method simulations and experimental verification through plasmonic near-field imaging, demonstrating its potential as a phase lens. The quadratic metalense design provides a practical solution for thin, lightweight, and low-power plenoptic systems with extensive field of view and broadband capabilities.

Our investigation focuses on the atmospheric pressure plasma discharges applied to large-scale surfaces within a confined system comprising six plasma sources and six plasma output zones connected via a closed network of high-voltage radio-frequency electrodes. This setup features a radio-frequency power supply operating at a frequency of 13 MHz, a maximum voltage of 600 V, and a maximum current of 100 A per electrode. Observations of the plasma source region reveal a self-organizing pattern characterized by the emergence of periodic structures, which can transition into chaotic states under certain conditions. The chaotic states are found to transition back to a more organized state as the system's complexity increases, resulting in the emergence of spatial structures. This transition is linked to the behavior of two small-scale structures, which can serve as an indicator of the system's complexity.

This research investigates the frequencies at which black holes with string corrections respond in higher dimensional spacetimes. The findings reveal a single exceptional mode, known as the quasi-normal mode, which is distinct due to its finite lifetime. The calculated frequencies align with previous mathematical approaches. The analysis also examines how the shape of silhouettes is impacted by including string corrections and varying the angle of observation.

Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) investigations into the stochastic gravitational wave background, particularly its background power-law slope, have traditionally relied on the "common-band" method. This involves correlating the gravitational wave signal with the cross-correlation of the pulsars' signals. We have developed a new approach, involving a second frequency shift, to isolate the gravitational wave signal. This method, known as "heterodyne heterodyne", allows us to eliminate common-mode noise and increase the signal-to-noise ratio of our results. We have simulated the performance of this method on mock PTA data and found that it outperforms the traditional common-band method in estimating the background's slope. In particular, the "heterodyne heterodyne" method can reduce errors significantly, from a few times 10^-4 to around 10^-5, particularly in cases with large signal-to-noise ratios.

In 2013, Ron Hansen introduced the concept of the support hypergraph to study the essential and sufficient criteria of MDS codes, and later in 2021, he proposed a simplified and more general approach using generator hypergraphs. These efforts led to the development of a new set of essential and sufficient criteria for generator matrices of MDS codes, which are rooted in the construction of generator hypergraphs. This approach is based on the principle that any generator matrix can be converted into an MDS code by modifying its corresponding generator hypergraph. This research aims to expand upon previous results by incorporating a new concept, the generator weighted hypergraph, to formalize a specific type of modification that can be applied to generator hypergraphs. By leveraging this concept, the study presents a new set of essential and sufficient criteria for generator matrices of MDS codes, and provides examples to demonstrate the practical application of these new criteria in various scenarios, including one where previous results are superseded by the novel findings.

This paper explores truncated Toeplitz operators with functions from a specific $p\cdot q$ lattice and examines how these operators can be extended to a matrix-valued form. A key aspect is identifying the kernels of these operators, followed by deriving a matrix-valued representation for functions from lattice-based kernels. Notably, this representation is equivalent to the matrix-valued truncated Toeplitz operator if the functions are restricted to rational polynomials.

This paper investigates Bayesian influence in sequential probability models. It begins by defining the concept of Bayesian influence in sequential probability spaces and examines its behavior in the context of zero-one trials. The analysis then focuses on sequential hypothesis testing, where the underlying model is based on a sequence of independent and identically distributed observations. By utilizing this framework, the researchers investigate Bayesian influence in sequential hypothesis testing, where the underlying model is grounded in a sequence of independent and identically distributed observations. They also delve into the relationship between Bayesian influence and average risk, specifically how the former affects the latter, as well as its behavior in sequential tests with regards to average risk.

In real-world applications, the effectiveness of an anomaly detection model often hinges on its ability to adapt to changes in data distribution. This adaptability is particularly crucial in scenarios where there is a shift in the data source, as evidenced by the challenges encountered in audio anomaly detection in diverse environmental settings. To address this issue, we propose a novel approach that leverages Universal Mapping (UMAP) to visualize audio data, making it easier to identify areas with anomalous patterns. By utilizing UMAP, we can pinpoint clusters that deviate from the normal range, as indicated by the locus with the lowest Euclidean distance from the data's normal distribution.

In a highly entangled system of SU(N) fermions at ultra-cold temperatures, a non-trivial phase emerges due to the presence of the Mott phase, which exhibits chiral order and a complex space of solutions. We investigate the emergence of this phase in a highly sparse, uniform gas of Mott droplets, transitioning into a state of coexistence with a highly entangled superfluid phase as the density of the gas decreases. Through a comprehensive analysis of this phase transition, we reveal that the system's behavior is accurately described by a specific model, known as the Nomadic ferromagnetism model, within a particular range. This model, which is based on the interaction between two species of localized bosons, provides a detailed explanation of the system's behavior and predicts a specific critical exponent that matches the one observed in the highly entangled phase. Furthermore, our study highlights the unique properties of this phase transition, which is characterized by the presence of a specific critical surface that is distinct from the highly entangled phase. We also find that the system's behavior is influenced by a specific type of critical exponent, known as the anomalous dimension, that is non-zero and positive. This unique behavior is a result of the system's transition from a state of coexistence to a highly entangled phase and is a direct consequence of the highly correlated nature of the Mott phase.

We've conducted a comprehensive study on 333 gamma-ray pulsars, utilizing a dataset from the third Fermi-LAT catalog. We derived 18 key properties for each source, then employed a machine learning approach to identify pulsars. A random forest classifier achieved 95% accuracy in pinpointing pulsars. Subsequently, we analyzed the precision of our classifier across various features and discovered that hardness ratio, latitude, and longitude were the most reliable indicators. We also found that pulsars in the low-energy band, characterized by hardness ratios below 0.4, predominantly reside within the galactic plane, while those outside this region fall in the extragalactic region. Conversely, pulsars in the high-energy band are dispersed throughout the sky. Interestingly, a third category exists with hardness ratios between these two groups, and these sources are concentrated near the galactic plane.

In this research, a theoretical study on the "fractional quantum point contacts" was conducted to investigate their transport properties when subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field. The investigation revealed numerous magnetorotons in the system's energy spectrum, which are caused by the interactions between the quantum fluctuations in the energy spectrum and the quantum fluctuations in the electron fluid's momentum. This interaction leads to a unique spectral regulation in the magnetotunneling spectra, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed quantum point contacts as a novel experimental platform for studying the complex physics of 1D strongly interacting systems.

The Intense Energy Occurrences experiment aims to study the occurrence of extremely energetic events in the positron spectrum.
A description of the experiment and its initial outcomes based on data from the Superconducting Super Collider is provided.
The experiment's results are compared with theoretical models that account for energy loss in the quantum electrodynamics framework.

The Cauchy problem for the truncated Boltzmann equation is investigated under minimal initial conditions with a degree of integrability, denoted as $f_0(x,v,t)=f_{0)(x,v)}$. Given that the collision frequency approaches zero as the domain size increases, we demonstrate the existence of a local solution in any given domain $\Omega_N(N \in \mathbb{N})$ within a time frame of $[0,1]$. This solution exhibits singular behavior at the domain boundary and is uniquely defined within that boundary domain.

To assess the reliability of machine learning classifiers under label corruption, we develop a set of experiments that evaluate their performance when training data is contaminated with inaccurate or intentionally misleading labels. The goal is to identify classifiers that can still produce accurate predictions even when presented with corrupted or manipulated input. To accomplish this, we developed the label corruption attack framework in PyTorch, allowing us to apply the attack across various datasets and models, and then assess the robustness of the models to label distortion under different attack scenarios.

This research focuses on the automorphism groups of non-trivial cyclic orbit codes, which we find to be isomorphic to the cyclic group of order p for p being a prime number. Furthermore, we identify connection patterns between the automorphism groups of parametric subcodes, primary codes, and their original code structures. Additionally, we have established the framework for the automorphism group to dictate the type of symmetry within cyclic orbit codes, either through reflection or rotation.

We establish a sufficient condition for the existence of non-trivial eigenfunctions for the complex Schrödinger operator $ \mathscr{L}_c = -d^2/dx^2+cx^\alpha$ with specific growth constraints on the complex parameter $c$. These conditions also ensure that complex eigenvalues will not be solely real.

To accurately model fluid dynamics, understanding the behavior of the particle mesh and the derivatives of smooth fields is essential. The most critical factor influencing the accuracy of these calculations is the smoothing length. While some techniques have been developed to address this issue, they come with increased computational costs. This paper proposes a new approach that leverages a mesh partition method to significantly enhance derivatives while maintaining a consistent smoothing length. Furthermore, it demonstrates the superiority of this method by comparing it to other techniques through a series of numerical experiments.

A novel, ground-breaking method for reconstructing high-quality spectral images from low-resolution color images is presented, utilizing an advanced model that combines deep learning and optimization techniques. This innovative approach, referred to as the Pixel-sensitive Deep Function-blend Network (P-DFN), features an external module that accurately recovers missing spectral details in low-resolution images and a pixel-sensitive optimizer that efficiently trains the model by selectively applying optimization techniques to specific image pixels. Through extensive testing on various datasets, including a real-world image dataset and synthetic data generated from a spectrometer, the P-DFN method has been found to significantly outperform previous state-of-the-art methods in producing high-quality spectral images.

In computer vision, the task of locating specific objects within large image collections, pinpointing their locations within a broader spatial framework, presents significant value and complexity. This paper introduces an innovative approach to address a challenging variant of this object detection problem, focusing on the identification of a particular object within an collection of outdoor images, accompanied by available location data. The proposed solution is designed to address key issues stemming from the co-occurrence of the target object and misleading background elements that can lead to incorrect localization. This novel method, grounded in the use of a probabilistic model, effectively integrates visual and spatial context information, thereby allowing for the flexible adaptation of its application across various categories of objects and diverse visual settings. An evaluation of the proposed solution was conducted using a comprehensive collection of image data sourced from Google Street View, featuring the objects from a list of 76 different types. The results of this evaluation demonstrate the substantial benefits of the proposed method in enhancing the accuracy of object detection and the incorporation of visual and spatial context, yielding a substantial improvement in performance, thereby making the identification of specific objects within large image collections, within a precise, geospatial framework, feasible.

Climate change has been closely linked to the acceleration of water cycle processes, leading to more frequent and severe flooding events.  In many cases, the issue stems from the removal of dams built for water control in the past, the decision to remove them now being a subject of debate.  In this research, a customized metric for detecting changes in reservoir storage capacity using time series analysis of satellite data related to water surface levels was developed.  The proposed method was applied to an area surrounding the dam of interest, identifying any changes in the water surface profile along rivers, lakes, and wetlands within its vicinity. Results showed high accuracy in the case of a specific dam in the United States, the Tarbela Dam on the Indus-Pakistan river, further validated through comparison with data from the US Army Corps of Engineers.

In number theory, researchers have extensively examined the properties of certain types of factorization.  Specifically, when a large composite number can be broken down into a specific small set of factors, this property is referred to as a k-resolvable number. Conversely, when a number can be decomposed into a minimal amount of distinct factor sets, this property is referred to as having few zones. QFS-zone refers to a type of factorization characteristic associated with a prime number q. Research has shown that certain numbers with a few zones can also possess this property. However, there is no established mathematical relationship that proves the existence of such numbers with a few zones. In an effort to address this knowledge gap, researchers have devised a method to identify and list all numbers that exhibit this property for a given prime number q. Moreover, when q is a prime number greater than 2, researchers have discovered that there exists an infinite number of such numbers with a few zones.

The Ad Copy Evaluation problem involves assessing the effectiveness of online ads using performance metrics like click-through rates, conversion rates, and cost per click. Initially, researchers focused on developing models that analyze text data, but recent studies have explored using multimedia content like images and videos for enhanced insights. This study examines the utility of point-of-attractiveness categories in evaluating ad copy performance. CAT variables are added to dataset samples from Google Ads and Display Advertisements, and researchers explore their impact using both text-only models and multimodal models. Interestingly, while text-only models perform well on standard metrics, they underperform when targeting CATs, whereas multimodal models excel across all metrics, including CATs. This suggests that incorporating multimedia information can improve predictions in this area.

Revealing crucial insights from a publicly available dataset, we investigated how shareholder confidence is impacted by market conditions. We tracked the 10-year market trend, discovering that the stock market has been in a state of relatively stable growth since 2018. Furthermore, we created a tool to visualize the share price behavior of individual companies, allowing analysis at the company level. Notably, we found that shares in technology companies tend to appreciate over the long term. Additionally, we explored the relationship between share price and earnings calls, observing a positive correlation over time. However, we also noted significant differences in share price reactions to earnings calls between 2018 and 2019, likely due to the global economic downturn and the COVID-19 pandemic. These findings have the potential to inform investment decisions and contribute to future research in the field.

In scenarios involving uniform sensor distribution, diverse sensors can be deployed to mitigate the impact of node failures. However, limited sensor mobility restricts the diversity of sensor placements. This research focuses on optimizing uniform sensor arrangements and diversity under restricted movement constraints. A novel approach is proposed to determine uniform sensor positions based on sensor node density and the maximum sensor mobility radius. For sensor diversity, an iterative algorithm is developed that alternates between optimizing sensor placement and node selection to maximize diversity. Two additional algorithms are also proposed to address node selection, the first selecting sensors with the most distant positions to maximize diversity and the second selecting sensors within a specified radius and angle to maintain uniformity. Experimental results indicate that the proposed algorithms significantly improve diversity for the same sensor configurations used in the study.

A novel eigenstate selection method has been developed, combining quantum information processing and numerical analysis. This technique is applied to resolve quantum eigenstate eigenvalues, specifically in solving linear systems of equations with complex matrices. This method incorporates a two-step process involving a polynomial construction and an adaptive search algorithm, enabling optimal sampling of eigenstates based on error estimates. Studies show that the method outperforms current eigenstate sampling methods in terms of circuit complexity, especially when dealing with sparse matrices. Furthermore, this technique can be used in conjunction with the phase estimation algorithm to provide accurate solutions for a range of parameter values, specifically when dealing with ill-conditioned matrices.

We examine compact solitons within the low-temperature gauged infant skyrmion model. This model, specifically for a two-component Bose-Einstein condensate, is characterized by an attractive interaction between components, governed by the parameter $\alpha$ in mm$^2$. The system's properties are influenced by a constant magnetic field and a Zeeman field strength $\beta$ and $\gamma$, where $\beta-\gamma$ determines the system's duality. In our analysis, we consider a non-linear material with a parameter $\mu$ that affects its structure. We identify a critical value of $\beta-\gamma$ above which the compact soliton ceases to exist. Furthermore, we investigate the impact of $\mu$ on the soliton's size, finding that increasing $\mu$ reduces the soliton's size, with a maximum allowable value of $\mu_{max}=\frac{2\beta\gamma}{3\kappa L}$, where $\kappa$ is a positive constant. Additionally, we explore the effect of $\beta-\gamma$ on the soliton's size, revealing that the compact soliton exists only when $\beta-\gamma$ is sufficiently large.

This research examines novel forms of particle interactions within the Standard Model's effective field theory framework and analyzes their implications at colliders. Specifically, the research looks at interactions involving the Higgs field, light bosons, and top quarks, which could explain the discrepancy between the predicted and measured Higgs mass and top quark mass. It uses data and projections from the LHC and future colliders to constrain these interactions and assess their potential impact. The research also explores the discovery potential of these interactions at the LHC, 100 TeV hadron colliders, and electron-positron colliders, including the CEPC, FCC-ee, and ILC, and finds that future colliders can significantly improve current constraints on these interactions.

We report the initial outcome of a project to create and characterize a rotating diamond nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) gyroscope. The project successfully implemented and tested a gyroscope comprising a diamond chip containing a nitrogen vacancy center with a diamond anisotropy field of 2.5 GHz, found to be resistant to operational magnetic interference. On a rotating platform, the NMR signal from a pair of diamond chips exhibited the predicted weak anisotropic modulation.

The development of the Oxberry cell has marked a significant milestone in the field of coarse-grained biomolecular simulation. The Oxberry model, which combines the Rotating Polar Wobble plane with the Correlated Transitions and Unfolding Dynamics, now offers a comprehensive framework for simulating the structure and behavior of ribosomes at atomic-level detail. The new framework has been applied to OxberryX, a software package designed to simulate ribosome dynamics, and its unique approach has been incorporated into the open-source code. The OxberryX code can be accessed through a GitHub repository.

Mobile object visual search is becoming increasingly significant, offering a way for users to identify objects using images taken by their smartphones. However, current solutions are limited as they demand high-quality images taken from a fixed perspective. To overcome this challenge, we propose a mobile multi-view object visual search system that enables users to search for objects using low-quality images taken from various angles. Our system is designed to provide a user-friendly interface by suggesting the most relevant views for the searched object. To achieve this, we employ a mobile query image analyzer to predict the object's 3D geometry and pose, which is then used to rank candidate views. We validate our approach by conducting experiments on the Oxford MultiView Dataset and a newly collected outdoor dataset, showcasing its effectiveness. The project is open-source and available on GitHub at https://github.com/DocDense/LightVOS.

A promising computing approach, Hyperdimensional (HD) computing, has shown potential in analyzing complex neurological data. We focus on seizures, a highly common condition that affects a significant portion of the population, which can only be diagnosed through advanced medical procedures. We utilize HD methods to analyze electroencephalogram data, aiming to identify seizure patterns that can aid in diagnosis. Our research demonstrates that with sufficient training data, HD models can effectively identify seizure patterns and maintain these associations even with minimal data, thus facilitating rapid identification of future seizures. We also demonstrate that using a single seizure to predict subsequent seizures further enhances the model's capabilities.

Future Deci-hertz gravitational-wave detectors are expected to discover thousands of binary black holes with masses in the range of 0.1-100 Msun, located at varying distances. By applying astrophysical priors to these detections, it's possible to derive independent constraints on the Hubble constant, $H_0$, from a sample of about 1,000 siren candidates with specific mass and redshift characteristics. However, this method's validity relies on understanding the distribution of binary black hole masses, which may be influenced by astrophysical factors. To maximize the siren's scientific potential, it's essential to develop a comprehensive model of binary black hole formation.

The QALD-9 dataset, comprising 1,655 queries in nine languages, has been defined by the QALD challenge, while its evolution into QALD-9-plus is characterized by the addition of more questions and the expansion of its coverage to ten more languages, as well as the extension of its scope to encompass two supplementary sources, WikidataS and DBpediaS. These two supplementary sources, DBpediaS and WikidataS, provide interpretations of questions in relation to DBpedia and Wikidata data sources respectively. The QALD-9-plus corpus, comprising a total of 2,514 questions, was compiled based on a thorough analysis of the linguistic properties of the questions and their potential answers. The corpus was further annotated with the answers to a set of questions, in order to provide a basis for the evaluation of the performance of question answering systems.

To enhance the reproducibility and integrity of scientific findings, it is crucial for researchers to have the ability to replicate and build upon previous studies. Although numerous tools are accessible for this purpose, it is frequently challenging for scientists to effectively utilize them due to a lack of knowledge and understanding. In an effort to bridge this gap, we are developing a collection of reusable R functions that can be utilized for a variety of data analysis tasks. This collection, which includes functions for common operations such as data cleaning and transformation, is intended to facilitate the resampling and renaming of data, thereby enabling scientists to revisit and build upon each other's research. By providing a standardized set of tools, we hope to promote greater transparency, reproducibility, and collaboration in data analysis.

Detecting bias in large image collections has become increasingly important across various domains, including medical imaging, due to its potential impact on fairness. Prior studies have proposed methods to measure bias based on image features and decisions, but these approaches are often limited because feature representations can be biased towards existing stereotypes, leading to unfair outcomes. In contrast, intrinsic bias detection focuses on data samples that are intentionally or unintentionally biased within the label distribution, without relying on external stereotypes. This approach aims to mitigate the negative consequences of bias while leveraging its benefits. We introduce a new framework for detecting intrinsic bias in medical images, which consists of three main components: (1) learning representations that capture label information to identify potentially biased samples; (2) employing a model to quantify the magnitude of intrinsic bias in images; and (3) utilizing a classifier to assess the direction of the bias. Our proposed method is then applied to two medical datasets to demonstrate its effectiveness.
